purpose: CC0 ground texture candidates to close the gap to Manor Lords (G0, third pass). Not downloaded into T/. Every id re-resolved against its API on 2026-10-01; every colour map viewed (cand_montage.jpg).
licence_note: Poly Haven: every asset CC0 1.0 (https://polyhaven.com/license). ambientCG: every asset CC0 1.0 (https://ambientcg.com/license). The manifest must record each source URL and licence (fetch_textures.py does this for Poly Haven today; ambientCG needs a zip path).
method:
G0 third pass: candidates.json. Run cand_fetch.py first (it resolves every id against its API, caches the colour maps
and writes cand_montage.jpg, which was viewed before the VIS verdicts below were written).

Predicting the ON-SCREEN colour of a candidate (fixes the second pass, which carried only hue across and compared albedo
saturation and value with on-screen targets):
  * model 'gain' (primary): per-channel linear-light gains, calibrated per layer and per view as
    mean linear screen RGB of our C7 crops / mean linear albedo RGB of the texture in that slot now (T/Textures/<L>/T_<L>_C.png).
    Applied per pixel to the candidate's colour map, re-encoded to sRGB, then measured exactly like the targets (hue_w, S, V).
    Views: rts80 (primary, what a player sees) and oblique (near-RTS) for grass; rts80 painted path (paint footprint) and the
    ground-level closeup path for dirt; oblique rock (cone + plateau cliff, no snow) and the rts80 cone (snow-painted top) for rock.
  * model 'ratio' (verifier): screen hue = albedo hue + offset; screen S = albedo S x (screen S / albedo S of the texture now);
    screen V likewise.
  * model 'offset' (second pass): hue only.
  * model 'neutral' (what-if): one grey gain per layer (screen linear luma / albedo linear luma), i.e. the same brightness
    but white-balanced light that neither warms nor saturates. C7's light does both (grass gains R 1.20, G 0.85, B 0.64 at
    rts80), so G1 may move toward this if it neutralises the sun/sky/tonemap; ranked separately.
  The spread between models and views is the stated uncertainty. All of it holds only under C7's lighting.
Required scalars = what a per-layer material tint would have to do to land on the target: hue shift (deg), saturation x, value x.
Distance d = sqrt((dHue/8)^2 + (dS/0.068)^2 + (dV/0.068)^2): the target's own in-crop spreads (8 deg, 0.068) as units.
cost_note: A candidate used as a straight replacement for the texture already in a slot (Grass, Dirt, Rock) costs no extra samples; per-layer tint, saturation and value scalars are ALU only. A candidate used as a second, noise-blended texture inside a slot adds 6 texture samples (C, N, ARH at two UV scales) wherever it shows; C7 sits at 2.96 ms against the 3.0 ms bar, so that needs a fresh terrain_gpu_ms measurement and probably a cut elsewhere.
